steps.title: Culture cells for protein extraction
steps.instruction: Grow the required cell lines in the specified media, incubate, and seed ~25 000 cells per well in a 24‑well plate for overnight attachment.

substeps.instruction: Culture HEK293T, MCF‑7, BJ‑5ta fibroblasts and HeLa in DMEM + 10 % v/v FBS; culture LNCaP in RPMI‑1640 + 10 % v/v FBS; culture HUVEC and PAOEC in EGM‑2; culture HCF in FGM‑2. Incubate all lines at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, humidified incubator in T25 flasks.
Wash cells gently with 5 mL DPBS at 25 °C, discard DPBS, add 500 µL TrypLE™ Express trypsin, agitate to spread, and incubate 37 °C for 3–5 min.
Add 2 mL appropriate culture medium to neutralize trypsin, pipette vigorously 3–5 times to obtain a single‑cell suspension.
Count cells using a Bright‑Line™ hemacytometer (inject 10 µL suspension).
Resuspend cells, pipette twice, and add a volume containing ~25 000 cells to one well of a 24‑well plate. Add culture medium to bring the well volume to 1 mL. Return plate to the incubator overnight.
For immunoprecipitation, note that ~80 % confluent 60 mm dish (human dermal fibroblasts) or 100 mm dish provides sufficient PIEZO1; for IP‑MS use at least two 150 mm dishes per condition.

steps.title: Prepare modified RIPA buffer and chill equipment
steps.instruction: Make 1× modified RIPA buffer, keep it on ice, and pre‑cool the 5425 R centrifuge and all tubes to 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: If avoiding TCEP‑NEM reaction, prepare RIPA without NEM and add 20 mM NEM later; optionally add 25 mM NaF and 1 mM Na₃VO₄ for phosphoprotein analysis.

steps.title: Extract proteins for western blotting
steps.instruction: Lyse cells in 100 µL modified 1× RIPA per well, collect lysate, and clarify by centrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Place the 24‑well plate on ice, discard media, add 100 µL 1× RIPA to each well, scrape with the back of a 10 µL tip if needed.
Transfer each well’s lysate to a pre‑cooled 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube on ice.
Spin at 13 000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Transfer supernatant to a new pre‑cooled 1.5 mL tube and incubate on ice for 30 min.

steps.title: Extract proteins for immunoprecipitation
steps.instruction: Lyse cells in ice‑cold IP lysis buffer, clarify, and keep lysate for downstream IP.

substeps.instruction: Prepare fresh 1× IP lysis buffer, pre‑cool the 5425 R centrifuge.
Place a 60 mm dish (or two 150 mm dishes for IP‑MS) on ice, discard media, wash once with cold PBS, add 500 µL (or 2 mL for 150 mm dishes) ice‑cold IP lysis buffer.
Lyse on ice for ≥30 min.
Spin at 13 000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Collect 450 µL supernatant (or 1.9 mL for IP‑MS) into a pre‑cooled tube.
Optional: freeze 20 µL of lysate at –80 °C as input (skip for IP‑MS).
Mix 10 µL Protein G Dynabeads with 1 µg PIEZO1 antibody and 430 µL lysate; rotate at 4 °C overnight (for IP‑MS use 30 µL beads, 6 µg antibody, 1.9 mL lysate).
Prepare fresh 1× IP wash buffer on ice.

steps.title: Wash and elute immunoprecipitated complexes
steps.instruction: Capture Dynabeads, wash three times, and elute bound proteins.

substeps.instruction: Place tubes on DynaMag™‑2 magnet, let beads bind 30 s.
Remove supernatant.
Add 500 µL (or 1 mL for IP‑MS) IP wash buffer, rotate at 4 °C for 10 min; repeat wash three times.
Remove wash buffer, add 20 µL ice‑cold 1× IP elution buffer.
Heat beads at 95 °C for 5 min (IP‑MS) or 60 °C for 5 min (western blot).
Collect eluate as IP fraction; load IP and input fractions at equal volumes on gel.

steps.title: Pre‑clear lysate for mass‑spectrometry IP (optional)
steps.instruction: Remove nonspecific binders before the main IP when performing IP‑MS.

substeps.instruction: Mix 30 µL Protein G Dynabeads with the cleared lysate, rotate overnight at 4 °C.
Spin at 13 000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C, discard pellet.
Filter supernatant through a Millex™ MCE 0.22 µm syringe filter.
Proceed with the standard IP steps starting at bead‑antibody incubation.

steps.title: Quantify total protein concentration
steps.instruction: Determine protein amount using a reducing‑compatible BCA assay and prepare samples for loading.

substeps.instruction: Take 2 µL of each lysate (skip for IP samples).
Perform Pierce™ BCA Protein Assay according to manufacturer, read absorbance at 562 nm on PHERAstarFS plate reader.
Mix 10–30 µg total protein with 20 % (v/v) 5× sample loading buffer on ice.
Note: for a 1–1.5 mm 10‑well gel, final sample volume ≤40 µL; for a 15‑well gel, ≤15 µL.

steps.title: Run SDS‑PAGE electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Separate proteins on a 3–8 % tris‑acetate gel using defined voltage program.

substeps.instruction: Load a 15‑well 3–8 % tris‑acetate mini‑gel into the gel tank.
Fill tank with running buffer so that wells are covered and buffer reaches the bottom opening.
Load each sample and 5 µL sharp pre‑stained protein ladder into wells, ensuring the tip reaches just above the well bottom.
Run at 80 V for 30 min, then increase to 110 V for 90 min until the dye front reaches the gel end.

steps.title: Transfer proteins to nitrocellulose membrane
steps.instruction: Perform wet transfer in a TE22 mini tank with cooling, avoiding bubbles.

substeps.instruction: Set up TE22 mini tank with refrigerated water bath and magnetic stirrer; pour transfer buffer to 1 cm below the max line.
Turn on pump and stirrer to pre‑cool the buffer.
Cut nitrocellulose to 6 × 7.5 cm and filter paper to 9 × 9 cm; assemble cassette, sponges, membrane, and paper, immerse all in transfer buffer at room temperature.
After electrophoresis, trim 2 mm off the gel bottom, open gel cage, and retrieve gel.
In transfer buffer, build sandwich: sponge‑paper‑gel‑membrane‑paper‑sponge, removing any trapped air bubbles.
Secure sandwich in cassette, place into TE22 tank, immerse in pre‑cooled buffer.
Run at constant current 300 mA for 140 min with cooling continuously on.

steps.title: Check transfer and block membrane
steps.instruction: Stain membrane with Ponceau S, then block with skim‑milk solution.

substeps.instruction: After transfer, cover membrane protein side with 2 mL 0.1 % w/v Ponceau S solution for 1 min; rinse with tap water until excess dye is removed. Red bands indicate successful transfer and can serve as total‑protein normalization.
Prepare blocking buffer: dissolve 300 mg skim milk powder in 10 mL TBS (pH 7.4).
Incubate membrane in blocking buffer on orbital shaker at 60–80 rpm either overnight at 4 °C or 1 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Incubate primary antibodies
steps.instruction: Apply PIEZO1 and α‑ACTININ primary antibodies to the blocked membrane.

substeps.instruction: Discard blocking buffer and briefly rinse membrane with tap water.
Dilute Novus PIEZO1 antibody (clone 2‑10) and Santa Cruz α‑ACTININ (H‑2) 1:1 000 in 5 mL TBS.
Incubate membrane on rocker for 1 h at room temperature or overnight at 4 °C (longer incubation for low PIEZO1 expression).

steps.title: First membrane wash
steps.instruction: Remove unbound primary antibody with two washes.

substeps.instruction: Wash membrane twice with 10 mL TBS containing 0.1 % v/v Tween 20, shaking at 80 rpm, 10 min each at room temperature.

steps.title: Incubate secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Apply fluorophore‑conjugated secondary antibody (or HRP alternative) to the membrane.

substeps.instruction: Prepare goat anti‑mouse IRDye 800CW (or equivalent) 1:10 000 dilution in 10 mL TBS with 0.02 % w/v sodium azide.
Incubate membrane on orbital shaker at 60 rpm, room temperature, for 40 min.

steps.title: Second membrane wash
steps.instruction: Remove excess secondary antibody and prepare membrane for imaging.

substeps.instruction: Wash membrane twice with 10 mL TBS + 0.1 % v/v Tween 20, shaking at 80 rpm, 10 min each at room temperature.
Store membrane in 1× TBS at 4 °C for no longer than one week if not scanning immediately.

steps.title: Scan membrane on LI‑COR Odyssey
steps.instruction: Acquire fluorescence images of the blot using appropriate laser settings.

substeps.instruction: Clean the Odyssey scanner surface with distilled water; keep membrane moist and place protein side down on the scanner, avoiding bubbles.
Scan at 700 nm (IR‑680) or 800 nm (IR‑800) depending on the secondary antibody; include the pre‑stained ladder for size reference.
After scanning, clean scanner surface with 70 % ethanol followed by distilled water, ensuring no liquid remains.

steps.title: Quantify band intensities
steps.instruction: Analyze scanned images with Image Studio software to obtain relative protein levels.

substeps.instruction: Import the image into Image Studio™.
Adjust angle and contrast using the free‑rotate tool and display panel.
Draw rectangular regions of interest (ROIs) for each band; use identical ROI size for the same protein across lanes.
Perform simple background subtraction via Analysis → Background → Median.
Record the intensity values displayed for each ROI; use these for normalization (e.g., PIEZO1 vs. α‑ACTININ).
